about: Idea cards for the venture board. Each seat is dealt three, from three different families, and answers its framings with them. A card is a forcing move: it pushes the seat away from the answer anyone would give. TRIZ principles are adapted to business; the separation principles resolve a contradiction; the business-model patterns and the eliminate-reduce-raise-create moves change what is sold and how; the trades are places to borrow a solution from.

cards.name: Segmentation
cards.prompt: Split the offer, the client or the work into parts that can be sold, priced or delivered on their own.

cards.name: Taking out
cards.prompt: Take out the one part of the work buyers value most and offer only that; or take out the part they dislike.

cards.name: The other way round
cards.prompt: Invert who does what: the client does what the firm does, the buyer comes to the seller, the end is delivered first.

cards.name: Prior action
cards.prompt: Do part of the work before anyone asks for it, so it is ready the moment a buyer needs it.

cards.name: Turn harm into benefit
cards.prompt: Take what hurts the business or its buyers (a risk, a delay, a loss, a weakness) and make it the offer.

cards.name: Self-service
cards.prompt: Let the system serve itself: the buyer, the product or the market does the work the firm now does by hand.

cards.name: Intermediary
cards.prompt: Put something between the firm and its buyers (a partner, a tool, a standard, a community) that does the selling or the trust-building.

cards.name: Cheap short-lived copies
cards.prompt: Replace something costly and lasting with many cheap, quick, disposable versions.

cards.name: Partial or excessive action
cards.prompt: When doing it exactly right is hard, do much more or much less of it, and see what that opens.

cards.name: Feedback
cards.prompt: Make results flow back continuously: to the buyer, to the firm, to the next buyer.

cards.name: Merging
cards.prompt: Join this offer with another firm's, or with a step the buyer does before or after, into one.

cards.name: Another dimension
cards.prompt: Move the offer to another level: from a project to a programme, from one client to a whole market, from a service to a standard.

cards.name: Separate in time
cards.prompt: Let both sides of the contradiction hold, at different moments: one before a point, the other after it.

cards.name: Separate in space
cards.prompt: Let both sides hold in different places: different pages, brands, audiences, channels or units.

cards.name: Separate on condition
cards.prompt: Let each side hold only when a condition is met: for some buyers, at some sizes, above some risk.

cards.name: Separate the part from the whole
cards.prompt: Let the whole have one property and its parts the opposite: a broad firm of narrow specialists, a fixed price made of variable parts.

cards.name: Subscription
cards.prompt: Sell an ongoing service for a regular fee instead of projects.

cards.name: Productise the service
cards.prompt: Turn a piece of repeated work into a named product with a fixed scope and price.

cards.name: Licensing
cards.prompt: Let others use what the firm built or knows, for a fee, without the firm doing the work.

cards.name: Freemium
cards.prompt: Give a useful part away to many, and sell the rest to the few who need more.

cards.name: Orchestrator
cards.prompt: Own the relationship and the result; let a network of others do the parts.

cards.name: Performance-based
cards.prompt: Get paid on the result the buyer cares about, not on the effort.

cards.name: Platform
cards.prompt: Bring two groups together and earn from the meeting, not from the work.

cards.name: Layer player
cards.prompt: Do one step of the chain for a whole industry, better than anyone does it for themselves.

cards.name: Data as the product
cards.prompt: Sell what the work teaches across many clients: a benchmark, an index, a dataset.

cards.name: Lock-in by usefulness
cards.prompt: Become the thing the buyer's daily work runs on, so leaving costs more than staying.

cards.name: Crowd and community
cards.prompt: Let the people who already know the firm create, sell or support for it.

cards.name: Equity for work
cards.prompt: Take part of the upside of the client's business in exchange for the work.

cards.name: Eliminate
cards.prompt: Which thing that every firm in this trade takes for granted could be removed entirely?

cards.name: Reduce
cards.prompt: Which thing could be reduced far below the trade's standard without buyers missing it?

cards.name: Raise
cards.prompt: Which thing could be raised far above the trade's standard, so far that buyers notice?

cards.name: Create
cards.prompt: Which thing that no firm in this trade offers could be created?

cards.name: How a hospital does it
cards.prompt: Triage, referrals, second opinions, specialists behind a generalist: borrow one.

cards.name: How a law firm does it
cards.prompt: Retainers, matters, partners who own a client, precedent shared across cases: borrow one.

cards.name: How a software company does it
cards.prompt: Free trials, versions, a public roadmap, self-serve onboarding: borrow one.

cards.name: How an insurer does it
cards.prompt: Pricing risk, pooling it, paying out when things go wrong: borrow one.

cards.name: How a franchise does it
cards.prompt: A proven playbook others run under one name, with the centre earning a share: borrow one.

cards.name: How a publisher does it
cards.prompt: An audience built first, sold to later; a list of titles; a season: borrow one.

cards.name: How a gym does it
cards.prompt: Membership, a habit, classes, a coach who checks in: borrow one.

cards.name: How a marketplace does it
cards.prompt: Ratings, guarantees, a fee per transaction, supply and demand balanced by the house: borrow one.
